title: Hard cases in the passive
intro: Read this before the difficult quiz. These traps hide in the verb type, not in the tense.

blocks.title: two objects
items: Verbs such as give, send, show, offer, tell and teach take two objects: She **gave** me a book.
Two passives are possible: **I was given** a book. / **A book was given** to me.
The person is usually the subject: **I was given** a book is more natural than *A book was given me*.

blocks.title: no passive
items: **Intransitive verbs** (no object) have no passive: happen, arrive, die, sleep, appear. *The accident was happened* is wrong. Say The accident **happened**.
**State verbs** such as have (possession), fit, suit, resemble and cost are not used in the passive: *A car is had by her* is wrong.

blocks.title: it is said that
items: **It is said / believed / thought / reported that** + clause: **It is believed that** the thief escaped.
The same idea with the person as subject: The thief **is believed to have escaped**. He **is said to be** rich.
**to be** for the same time as the main verb, **to have + participle** for an earlier time.

blocks.title: get and have
items: **get + past participle** is informal and describes something that happens to you: She **got hired**. The vase **got broken**.
**have + object + past participle** is a service done for you: I **had** my hair **cut**. She **is having** her car **repaired**.
Use the real participle: *I had my hair cutted* is wrong. Say **cut**.

blocks.body: Before you build a passive, check that the active verb has an object. No object, no passive.

builds: Turning an active sentence into the passive
